authorizedBy: docs/post-3f2-generalization-architecture-decision.json section 11 (recommended package/version architecture) - additive OperativeDocumentResolution concept, no schema migration, generalized restatement-reference regex, fallback wired into real production call sites
establishedRootCausesRestated: B1: relationship-resolution.ts's AGREEMENT_REF_RE required the reference label to sit immediately after 'the'/'that certain', missing the equally standard recital phrasing ('The Borrower and Lender are parties to A Credit Agreement dated as of...') that begins with 'a'/'an'.

B2: document-identity.ts already extracts a broader originalAgreementReferenceHint that was not being reused by relationship-resolution.ts, risking two competing parsers - addressed by fixing the shared AGREEMENT_REF_RE itself (generalizing the single resolution rule) rather than building a second parser.

B3: computeOperativeContractState already had a purpose-built fallback (unresolvedTargetEffectsForThisInstrument) that was not wired into the real orchestrator.ts production call site - the exact root cause of the original Riot 'OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED with 0 provisions' false-clean-status bug.
B4: even a perfectly-resolved restatement chain lacked any consumer-level concept for 'which whole document currently governs' - addressed additively via OperativeDocumentResolution.
explicitlyNotDone: No Prisma migration (schema unchanged - git diff against production-freeze SHA on prisma/** is empty)
No Riot-specific recital text, section numbers, or party names encoded anywhere in production logic
No second/duplicate agreement-reference parser - the existing single resolution rule (resolveAgreementReference) was generalized in place

No PROVISION_EFFECT_RESOLUTION_STATUS vs DOCUMENT_VERSION_RESOLUTION_STATUS split - code did not prove OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED was overloaded in a way requiring separation; the additive operativeDocument field coexists with the pre-existing status field without redefining it

unitB1_regexGeneralization.change: AGREEMENT_REF_RE determiner alternation widened from (?:the|that certain) to (?:the|that certain|an?) - adds ordinary English determiners 'a'/'an' immediately before the agreement-label alternation, generalizing to recital-style self-references ('parties to a Credit Agreement dated as of...') without any package-specific text.
unitB1_regexGeneralization.domainGenerality: Both determiners are ordinary English grammar, not tied to any specific drafting convention, party name, or section number. Verified generic via B2's synthetic Zenith Robotics/Meridian Capital fixture (never Riot/Coinbase text).

unitB2_dateAmbiguitySafeguard.rationale: A restatement's recital conventionally quotes the ORIGINAL agreement's own execution date even on a second-or-later restatement (a real, generic drafting convention, not Riot-specific) - direct type+date matching against that quoted date would silently resolve to the wrong (too-old) predecessor.
unitB2_dateAmbiguitySafeguard.mechanism: SUPERSEDING_QUALIFIER_RE detects the generic phrase 'as amended and restated as of...' near a reference (any ordinal, never a specific one). When present, resolveAgreementReference skips direct date matching and instead falls back to chronological-predecessor resolution: the most recent OTHER same-type document dated strictly before the source document's own execution date.
unitB2_dateAmbiguitySafeguard.confidenceDiscipline: This inferential resolution is deliberately capped at status REVIEW_REQUIRED / confidence 0.7 - never silently promoted to a confident RESOLVED - and returns UNRESOLVED (target null) when zero or more than one same-type prior candidate exists (never guessed under real ambiguity or genuine absence of evidence).

unitB3_confidencePropagationFix.selfDiscoveredGap: Not explicitly named in the architecture decision - discovered while implementing B2. deterministic-parser.ts's isFullRestatement branch previously computed status/confidence from a flat target-present binary (targetDocumentId ? RESOLVED/0.9 : REVIEW_REQUIRED/0.3), which would have silently promoted a REVIEW_REQUIRED/0.7 chronological-predecessor resolution (or a pre-existing REVIEW_REQUIRED/0.55 type-only-match resolution) to a false-confident RESOLVED/0.9 amendment effect merely because SOME targetDocumentId was non-null.
unitB3_confidencePropagationFix.fix: DeterministicParseInput.restatementTargetResolution now carries the full relationship-candidate resolution object (status/confidence/unresolvedReason) verbatim instead of two flat fields; parseDeterministicAmendmentEffects derives the effect's own status/confidence/unresolvedReason directly from it. pipeline.ts's restatesEdge lookup was changed from an arbitrary .find() to a status/confidence-ranked best-candidate selection (RESOLVED > REVIEW_REQUIRED > UNRESOLVED, then higher confidence), needed once a document can carry multiple RESTATES-type candidates from both the caption-style and recital-style regex paths.

unitB4_operativeDocumentConcept.newType: OperativeDocumentResolution (lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/types.ts) - { status: RESOLVED | REVIEW_REQUIRED | NOT_APPLICABLE, operativeDocumentId, predecessorDocumentIds, relationshipChain, reviewReason }. Deliberately omits effectiveDate/provenance as top-level fields beyond what relationshipChain's own per-edge effectiveDate already carries - kept to the smallest additive shape the mission's own required fields support without inventing unused structure.
unitB4_operativeDocumentConcept.newFunction: computeOperativeDocument(baseDocumentId, allEffects, unresolvedRestatementEffects) in chain.ts - a generic directed-graph algorithm over RESTATE_AGREEMENT effects (successor restates predecessor). Handles arbitrary chain depth (demonstrated: 3-document), forks (two documents claiming to restate the same predecessor -> REVIEW_REQUIRED), cycles (-> REVIEW_REQUIRED), and disconnected chains (-> REVIEW_REQUIRED). NOT_APPLICABLE when the instrument has no restatement activity at all, or when its own base document is not part of the resolved restatement graph.
unitB4_operativeDocumentConcept.resolutionThreshold: A restatement effect only blocks the document-graph resolution when it has NO target document at all (status UNRESOLVED, targetDocumentId null - a genuinely unknown link). A REVIEW_REQUIRED effect WITH a real targetDocumentId (e.g. the B2 chronological-predecessor inference) still names a concrete document and is used to build the graph - the underlying effect's own REVIEW_REQUIRED status already flags that specific provision-level effect for human confirmation (a separate concern), while the document-identity GRAPH itself can still be unambiguous (a single linear chain, no forks, no missing links) and therefore RESOLVED at the document level.
unitB4_operativeDocumentConcept.wiring: operative-state.ts's computeOperativeContractState calls computeOperativeDocument(input.baseDocumentId, input.allEffects, input.unresolvedTargetEffectsForThisInstrument ?? []) and returns the result as the new optional operativeDocument field on OperativeContractState - deliberately uses input.allEffects (not the targetInstrumentKey-filtered instrumentEffects), since a restatement's target commonly resolves to a DIFFERENT instrument key than its own document's instrument.
unitB4_operativeDocumentConcept.productionWiring: lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts's analyzeInstrument now computes unresolvedTargetEffectsForThisInstrument = amendmentResult.effects.filter(e => e.target.targetInstrumentKey === null) and passes it into computeOperativeContractState - closing the exact gap where the pre-existing escape hatch existed but was never reached by the real production call path (only by unit tests invoking computeOperativeContractState directly).

antiOverfittingCompliance: Unit B1/B2's regexes generalize on ordinary English grammar and a generic ordinal-restatement drafting phrase, never any Riot-specific text, section number, party name, or date. Verified via the automated benchmark-string grep in the shared gate and by the wholly-synthetic Zenith Robotics/Meridian Capital/Cascade Textiles/Union Point Lender test fixtures in tests/contract-model/post-3f2-package-graph-restatement.test.ts, which deliberately mirror Riot's structural shape (a 3-document restatement chain with a second-restatement recital quoting the original date) while using 100% invented content.
